description: Portal X es un equipo enfocado en el desarrollo de una aplicación web que integra y armoniza los datos de focos de incendios activos registrados por los satélites MODIS y VIIRS. Su objetivo es facilitar la visualización de la actividad de incendios mediante un calendario que permita identificar patrones históricos, detectar situaciones inusuales y reconocer períodos de mayor riesgo, contribuyendo a mejorar la prevención, el monitoreo y la respuesta ante emergencias ambientales.
summary:
MODIS (since 2000, about 1 km) and VIIRS (about 375 m) both detect active fires, but their records cannot be compared directly: VIIRS sees smaller fires, so it reports far more hot spots, and the two sensors describe confidence differently. In our Colombia data (2015-2025), adding VIIRS (NOAA-20, from April 2018) makes total detections jump about six times from 2017 to 2019, while MODIS alone grows only about 1.2 times.

FireTrack Colombia puts both NASA FIRMS records on one footing and shows them as a burning activity calendar. Every detection is converted to a common structure, confidence is mapped to three shared classes (low, nominal, high), and same-day detections within about 5 km are grouped so one fire is not counted twice. Users explore more than one million detections across Colombia's 33 departments with an interactive map, a day-by-day calendar, a seasonality chart, a yearly comparison and a list of critical days, in Spanish and English.

The app runs in any browser, including phones, with no installation. It helps early warning teams, emergency responders and land managers see where and when burning repeats, so they can prepare before the peaks.
details:
FireTrack Colombia is a bilingual (Spanish and English) web dashboard that turns two incompatible NASA FIRMS fire records into one burning activity calendar. MODIS (about 1 km pixels) and VIIRS (about 375 m pixels) detect fires differently, and our data shows the problem clearly: MODIS runs alone from 2015 to 2017, and when VIIRS (NOAA-20) joins in April 2018 the raw total jumps about six times between 2017 and 2019, while MODIS alone grows only about 1.2 times. In every full year since 2019, VIIRS reports about 4.2 times more detections than MODIS, so raw counts say more about the sensor than about the fire.

We processed more than one million detections from 2015 to 2025 into one common structure (date, time, location, sensor, confidence and fire radiative power). Because MODIS gives confidence as a number and VIIRS as categories, we mapped both to three shared classes (low, nominal, high). We also grouped same-day detections within about 5 km into one unique hot spot, so a fire seen by both satellites is not counted twice. We treat each detection as a thermal anomaly, not a confirmed wildfire.

Instead of tables of coordinates, users get an interactive map of Colombia's departments, a day-by-day calendar, a seasonality chart, a yearly comparison and a ranked list of critical and unusual days. This makes the fire season readable at a glance: about two thirds of detections fall between January and March, and two departments, Vichada and Meta, hold about 37%. Early warning teams, emergency responders and land managers can reinforce surveillance before the peak months and review unusual days quickly.

The app is built with HTML, JavaScript and SVG in a single self-contained page hosted on GitHub Pages. All filtering and charts run in the browser, so it needs no server or installation, works on a phone or a standard laptop, and can be shared as a simple link with field teams that have poor connectivity. The app is built with HTML, JavaScript and SVG in a single self-contained page hosted on GitHub Pages. We used GPT (OpenAI) to help build the web page and Claude (Anthropic) to help with data analysis, the slides and text drafting. All filtering and charts run in the browser, so it needs no server or installation, works on a phone or a standard laptop, and can be shared as a simple link with field teams that have poor connectivity.

This version covers MODIS from 2015 and VIIRS from April 2018, through 2025. Our next steps are to extend the record back to 2000, add earlier VIIRS data, calibrate VIIRS to MODIS on the overlap period, and add near real-time alerts.
